neighbours.label: In health or safety advice, the subject word (usually 'you', sometimes 'there') of a clause about a condition or risk someone only suspects or might have, e.g. right after 'if you think/suspect/feel' or 'when there is a chance'; fires on the subject before its verb, quiet for the same subject in plain statements or ordinary if/when conditions
fire: If you think you may have broken a bone, keep the limb still and seek medical help.
If you suspect you have food poisoning, drink plenty of fluids and rest.
Call your doctor right away if you feel you might be having an allergic reaction.
If you think you have been exposed to carbon monoxide, get outside into fresh air immediately.
When there is a chance you could be pregnant, avoid taking this medication without advice.
If you suspect you might have a concussion, do not drive or return to sports that day.
Seek emergency care if you think you are having a heart attack.
If you feel you may be dehydrated, sip water slowly and stay out of the sun.
quiet: Spit out any excess mucus that enters your mouth as a result.
We know you are in danger, so stay inside.
You have broken a bone, so keep the limb still and seek medical help.
You have food poisoning, so drink plenty of fluids and rest.
Call your doctor right away if you need a refill of your prescription.
If you are going camping, pack a carbon monoxide detector for the heater.
When you are pregnant, your doctor will review your medications with you.
If you play contact sports, wear a properly fitted helmet.

predictions: Blind test written from the label only. Expect most fire items to peak on the second 'you' (0.4-0.6); quiet items near 0, the solver's mucus/danger leak texts below 0.1 on their own.
notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L33/N6480+ (French subject end before its verb); the downstream drop was only 0.01, and this reader's label is about English health advice, not French syntax. Feeders-first arm: top feeders were unlabelled (L9/N6716- question marks in FAQ text; L32/N7539+ subject before 'may', suppresses 'possibly/likely'). The pole's output promotes ' may'/' might'.
